page: Amazon Web Services r8id.4xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor built on the x86_64 architecture. It features 16 virtual CPUs across 8 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, running at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz. The processor includes a substantial 480 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. It is equipped with 128.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory operating at 7 GHz, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core.

This instance includes 950 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage, providing fast local read and write capabilities. Network performance is supported by an 8 Gbps baseline bandwidth. The underlying Nitro hypervisor manages the dedicated CPU allocation. The Intel Xeon processor supports advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for tile and INT8 operations, alongside hardware-accelerated cryptography via AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

Benchmarks indicate strong single-threaded performance, with Geekbench single-core scores and gzip compression rates placing in the top 25%. Text processing performance is highly efficient, ranking in the top 10%. Memory bandwidth tests show 1282.27 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 115.87 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. For database and key-value operations, the instance handles 30.14 million Redis SET operations per second and achieves a Passmark database score of 8936.44. While it lacks a dedicated GPU, its AMX instructions enable efficient CPU-based machine learning, achieving a top-tier 339.94 tokens per second for small LLM text generation. This profile makes the r8id.4xlarge highly suitable for memory-intensive databases, caching layers, text processing pipelines, and local-storage-dependent enterprise applications.
